facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered near Dapingfang in Chaoyang County, Liaoning, China, within the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype of Piscivorenantiornis (IVPP V22582), was discovered near Dapingfang in Chaoyang County, Liaoning, China, in sediments identified as belonging to the Jiufotang Formation.

facts.statement: A second specimen of the species was described in 2020.
facts.quote: A second specimen of P. inusitatus (IVPP V23362) was described in 2020.

facts.statement: Piscivorenantiornis was a small bird belonging to the Enantiornithes group.
The skull preserves a pair of craniolateral processes that are absent in most other enantiornithines.
facts.quote: It preserves a pair of craniolateral processes absent in most other enantiornithines.

facts.statement: The pubic boot is large with a tip that is strongly recurved.
facts.quote: The pubic boot is large and its tip is strongly recurved.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the fish bone arrangement represents a gastric pellet regurgitated shortly before the bird's death.
facts.quote: Due to its shape and proximity, and a lack of fish bones elsewhere on the slab, it is believed that this structure represents a gastric pellet that was regurgitated shortly prior to its death.

facts.statement: The fossil range is the Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage).
The animal lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: In its original description, the genus nested either alongside Pterygornis or outside a clade containing Pterygornis and Dunhuangia.
facts.quote: In the paper describing Piscivorenantiornis, it nested either alongside Pterygornis, or outside of a clade comprising Pterygornis and Dunhuangia.

facts.statement: A later study recovered the genus outside of a clade comprising Mirusavis and Shangyang.
facts.quote: In a paper published four years later, it was recovered in outside of a clade comprising Mirusavis and Shangyang.

facts.statement: The genus name means "fish-eater" in Latin, marking it as the first known piscivorous enantiornithine.
facts.quote: Piscivoreantiornis genus name is derived from the Latin piscis ("fish") and vorare ("to eat"), denoting it as the first known piscivorous enantiornithine

rejected.statement: The holotype was found alongside a spindle-shaped arrangement of fish bones likely belonging to the genus Lycoptera.
rejected.quote: The holotype of Piscivorenantiornis was found alongside a spindle-shaped arrangement of fish bones, likely belonging to the genus Lycoptera.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'was found alongside a spindle-shaped arrangement of fish'
